purpose: Bus-programmed SPI host controller: software writes configuration and TX/chip-select words through a TX FIFO, a shift-register engine clocks bytes out on spi_dat_o/spi_clk_o to the device chosen by spi_csn_o while sampling spi_dat_i, and received bytes are returned to software through an RX FIFO, with a status register and an interrupt.

flows.value: SPI unit configuration: enable, clock mode (cpol, cpha), clock rate (prsc, cdiv, highspeed) and interrupt enables

conceptual_assets.name: CA1 SPI unit configuration (enable, clock mode cpol/cpha, clock rate prsc/cdiv/highspeed)
conceptual_assets.flow: F1 configure; F2 disable / abort; F6 serial clock generation

C.why: Read back to any bus reader at L153-158, but mode and divider values carry no secret; disclosure changes nothing in this module.

I.why: L140-145 overwrite every field on any bus write with stb=1, rw=1, addr(2)=0 (L137-139); no other condition (bus_req_i.priv and .src are never read). enable=0 clears both FIFOs (L211, L243) and aborts the engine (L281, L331-333); cpol/cpha move the sampling edges (L286, L301, L309, L320, L324); prsc/cdiv/highspeed set the bit rate (L371-372).

A.why: spi_clk_en is produced only when enable=1 and (clkgen_i(prsc)=1 or highspeed=1) and cdiv_cnt=cdiv (L369-373); every engine step waits on it (L299, L308, L317). A prsc value whose clkgen_i bit never pulses leaves the engine in state "101" with busy=1 (L340) forever.

U.why: ctrl.enable=0 is an implemented override: state(2) follows it every cycle (L281) so the "others" arm (L329-333) aborts any transfer mid-byte and drops chip select (L332), and the FIFOs are cleared (L211, L243). ctrl.highspeed (L371) bypasses the prescaler selection.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: One bus write to the control register with bit 0 cleared (L140) empties both FIFOs (L211, L243) and deasserts spi_csn_o (L281 -> L332 -> L352) in the middle of a device command; a write that flips cpol (L142) while a device is still selected toggles spi_clk_o in the idle arm (L286 -> L344), giving the device a spurious clock edge.

conceptual_assets.name: CA2 transmit data (bytes and commands sent to the selected device)

C.why: The byte is held in rtx_engine.sreg (L292) and driven on spi_dat_o (L343) without any dependence on spi_csn_o (L352-354); TX bytes can carry secrets written to a flash or secure element.

I.why: Any bus write with stb=1, rw=1, addr(2)=1 enqueues a word (L212-213) with no privilege check; the engine loads the oldest word (L292) and shifts it out (L318, L343). An injected or altered byte becomes part of the command the device executes.

A.why: tx_fifo.clear = not ctrl.enable (L211) discards every queued byte; each bit waits on spi_clk_en (L299, L308, L317).

U.why: The only mode switch on this path is the command tag (L289), which is normal use; no line bypasses or forces the TX byte.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: A foreign DATA write (L212-213) queued between the driver's bytes is loaded into sreg (L292) and clocked out on spi_dat_o (L343) to whichever device cs_ctrl selects, changing the command or payload the device receives.

conceptual_assets.name: CA3 receive data (bytes returned by the selected device)

C.why: L174 returns rx_fifo.rdata(7:0) to any bus read with stb=1, rw=0, addr(2)=1 (L137-138, L152, L173) and L246 pops it; nothing reads bus_req_i.priv or .src. Also, after the last shift (L318) the received byte stays in sreg, not cleared by the idle or disable arms (L284-295, L329-333), so its bit 7 stays on spi_dat_o (L343) until the next TX load (L292).

I.why: spi_dat_i is sampled with no check (L310), shifted in (L318) and written to the RX FIFO when done pulses (L245, L321); wrong cpol/cpha (L141-142) samples on the wrong edge.

A.why: rx_fifo.we = done (L245) writes whether or not the FIFO has room: rx_fifo.free is never read (only its connection at L236), so a full RX FIFO loses bytes without a status bit; rx_fifo.clear = not ctrl.enable (L243) discards unread bytes.

U.why: No mode bypasses the read path; the read is gated only by the bus decode at L246 and L152.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: Any bus master that reads the data address (L246) pops the device's reply and receives it on bus_rsp_o.data (L174), e.g. bytes read from a flash or secure element, and the owning driver never sees that byte; the MSB of the last received byte also stays on the external data output (L343).

conceptual_assets.name: CA4 chip-select selection (which external device is addressed)

C.why: Only cs_ctrl(3) (a device is selected) is exported to the bus (L171); the selection is visible on the pins by design.

I.why: A DATA write with bus bit 31 set (L213) becomes a command word at the FIFO output (L289) and loads cs_ctrl (L290); cs_ctrl(3) and cs_ctrl(2:0) drive one spi_csn_o line low (L353-354). No privilege check on the write (L212).

A.why: ctrl.enable=0 forces state(2)=0 (L281) and the "others" arm clears cs_ctrl (L332), deselecting the device mid-transfer; reset clears it (L275).

U.why: All eight index values are legal at L354; no line overrides the selection except the disable path already counted under A.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: An injected command word (bus bit 31 = 1) moves spi_csn_o (L354) to another device index, so the following data bytes (L292, L343), such as an erase or write command, reach a device the driver never meant to address.

conceptual_assets.name: CA5 serial clock waveform presented to the device

C.why: The clock carries no data value.

I.why: sck is computed from cpol/cpha in every arm (L286, L301, L309, L320, L324, L331). In the idle arm sck follows ctrl.cpol every cycle (L286) while cs_ctrl keeps a device selected, so a control write that flips cpol (L142) makes an extra edge on spi_clk_o (L344) with the device selected: one inserted bit in its command stream.

A.why: sck advances only on spi_clk_en (L299, L308, L317), which depends on the configuration in CA1 (L369-373).

U.why: highspeed (L371) changes the rate but is counted under CA1.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: Flipping cpol during an idle gap with chip select held (L142 -> L286 -> L344) clocks one extra bit into the selected device and shifts every later bit of its command.

conceptual_assets.name: CA6 interrupt configuration and request

C.why: Enable bits are read back (L164-167) but carry no secret.

I.why: Any control write overwrites the four enables (L146-149). Clearing irq_rx_avail removes the only notification of received data (L256); with rx_fifo.free unread (CA3 A), bytes are then lost.

A.why: irq_o is blocked whenever ctrl.enable=0 or an enable is cleared (L255-259), and is held high by irq_tx_empty=1 with an empty TX FIFO (L257): a continuous interrupt to the CPU.

U.why: No override beyond the enable gate at L255.

conceptual_assets.attack_effect: Setting irq_tx_empty (L147) with an empty TX FIFO holds irq_o high (L257) and keeps interrupting the CPU; clearing irq_rx_avail (L146) silences the RX notification (L256).

hypotheses: No access control in this module: bus_req_i.priv and bus_req_i.src arrive with every request but are never read (only L25), and bus_rsp_o.err is constant 0 (L133). Any master or privilege level that can reach the address can reconfigure, inject TX or chip-select words and read RX data. Whether that is a vulnerability depends on address protection outside this module.

Status side channel: busy, chip-select-active and FIFO flags (L160-172) are readable by any bus reader and reveal SPI activity of another software context; the harm depends on a multi-tenant system outside this module.

Residual data in the FIFO memories: both FIFOs are instantiated with FULL_RESET => false (L192, L224); clear (L211, L243) may reset only pointers and leave old TX/RX bytes in the sub-block memory. Not visible here.
RX overflow behaviour: FIFO_SAFE => true (L191, L223) suggests a write to a full FIFO is dropped inside the sub-block; the loss mechanism is in the sub-block, not visible here.
What the connected devices are (boot flash, secure element, TPM) decides how severe CA2/CA3/CA4 are; the module source says nothing about them.

Fault injection on rtx_engine.state into state "101" without a FIFO load would shift out the stale sreg, which after a transfer holds the last received byte (L318, L343), to the selected device. Requires a fault model outside the source.
clkgen_en_o (L383) tells an external clock generator to run; what that generator does when it drops is outside this module.

map_assessment.used_for: Indexing all 66 elements (26 port entries, 40 signal entries); reading SOURCES/DERIVES_FROM/CARRIES/COPIES as data edges and GATES/SELECTS/CONSTRAINS as control edges to build flows F1-F9; finding elements with no local use (bus_req_i.priv/src and six other request fields, rx_fifo.free, rx_fifo.half); storage kind (24 edge-stored elements); constant drivers (err = 0, csn defaults); and chaining ctrl.enable -> rtx_engine.state (L281) -> SELECTS cs_ctrl (L332) to find the disable/abort path.
map_assessment.insufficient_for: Anything through the two FIFO sub-blocks: the map has no edge from tx_fifo.wdata to tx_fifo.rdata or from rx_fifo.wdata to rx_fifo.rdata, so it cannot show that bus_req_i.data(31) becomes the command tag tx_fifo.rdata(8) that decides chip-select versus data (had to read L213 and L289). It also cannot say what the FSM states mean (load, shift, abort); that the same sreg holds TX then RX data and leaves the received MSB on spi_dat_o between transfers (had to read L292, L318, L343 together); or that the idle arm drives sck from cpol every cycle while chip select stays asserted (L286 with L290/L332). The functionality hints never decided anything.
map_assessment.errors_found: All 473 occurrence texts match their source lines. One hint error: rx_fifo.re is described as a read-enable output of the RX FIFO, but it is the FIFO input re_i driven by this module (L238, L246). Labelling choice, not an error: the OR operands at L172 (rtx_engine.busy, tx_fifo.avail) are recorded as GATES of bus_rsp_o.data, per the single-bit-operand convention, though they are status values.

process_notes: 1. Read the prompt, then the whole source (small). 2. Parsed the map with Python, checked all 473 occurrence texts against the source lines (0 mismatches), and printed a per-element index of edges, storage, constants and connections. 3. Stated purpose from ports and source: a bus-programmed SPI host controller with TX/RX FIFOs, a chip-select command path, a clock divider and an interrupt. 4. Listed flows F1-F9 and traced each along map edges; confirmed each edge on its line. 5. Queried for elements with no local use and for incoming edges to the output ports. 6. Answered the four questions per value with a mechanism line, then assigned roles. Where the map changed a decision: (a) the empty relationship lists of bus_req_i.priv/src confirmed there is no privilege check in the module, which made I and C "yes" for bus-writable and bus-readable values rather than hypotheses about a trusted bus; (b) rx_fifo.free having only a connection showed that received bytes are written without checking room (CA3 A); (c) the ctrl.enable CARRIES rtx_engine.state edge plus state SELECTS cs_ctrl at L332 showed the disable path drops chip select. Where the map was insufficient and the source was read instead: the FIFO crossing (L213 -> L289), the dual use of sreg and the received MSB left on spi_dat_o (L292, L318, L343), and the cpol-driven idle clock edge (L286). Role rules applied: data operands (SOURCES/DERIVES_FROM/COPIES/CARRIES) into a register -> stores; the input port whose bits become the value -> sets; input ports that only gate -> secondary; a signal that assembles a new word from several sources -> computes; a signal that only forwards one source (rx_fifo.wdata = 0 & sreg) -> secondary; the output-side signal of a sub-block FIFO -> stores, because the FIFO storage is invisible and that signal is where the stored value reappears.
